title: Set Up Your Accounts and Explore Linux
text:
3.3 Sleek Out Linux Mint






TipLEVEL 4+: MAKE THE INSTRUCTIONS BETTER



If anything here is unclear, incomplete, or could be explained better, improve it in your own copy. Use Suggesting mode if it is available. Otherwise, add a clearly labelled “Suggested improvement” with your revised wording. Include one sentence explaining why your version is clearer or more useful. Do not remove required work. Mr. A will review your change and may update the course website and future assignment documents if he agrees it helps. Improving a real instruction accurately is one way to demonstrate Level 4+ thinking.



Part 2: make Linux feel like your computer






NoteCinnamon or Xfce? Check before following appearance instructions



Linux Mint Cinnamon and Linux Mint Xfce use different settings. Run echo "$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP" in Terminal. Use the Cinnamon script only when the result includes Cinnamon, and use the Xfce script only when it includes XFCE. Never force the wrong script to run.








ImportantOpen the assignment and know what to submit



Make a copy of 3.3 Sleek Out Linux Mint.
Submit ONE completed Google Doc in Google Classroom. It must contain a BEFORE screenshot, an AFTER screenshot, the configuration detective response, and all five short reflection answers. Do not attach the screenshots as separate files.
The handout was originally written around Xfce. Cinnamon students complete the same evidence and reflection using the Cinnamon controls and script identified on this page.




1. Save your BEFORE screenshot
Do this before changing any settings. Sign in to your own Linux account and show the full desktop with its wallpaper and bottom panel visible. Press Print Screen (PrtSc). If nothing happens, try Fn + PrtSc or search the application menu for Screenshot. Save the picture in your Pictures folder and insert it into the assignment Google Doc.






NoteWhat a clear BEFORE screenshot looks like






A typical Linux Mint Xfce desktop before customization, with the wallpaper and full panel visible.


Show the whole desktop, not a cropped corner. Keep the wallpaper and full panel visible. This reference image is not a student submission. Image source: Linuxiac.




2. Get inspiration from Xfce makeovers
Watch the parts that interest you. Use the built-in settings in the next section. You do not need to copy either design, download a theme, run terminal commands, or install Compiz.



Customize Your Linux Mint XFCE: A Simple Guide by Specter-3924 shows a complete Linux Mint Xfce desktop makeover.



Making XFCE Look Better by NH Soft: start at 3:33 for wallpaper, 7:32 for themes, and 12:49 for the panel. Skip downloads, terminal commands, and the later Compiz effects.



Three realistic built-in-only design ideas
Pick one direction or mix ideas. Theme names can vary slightly between classroom computers.









Design direction
Wallpaper
Theme or icons
Panel




Calm study desktop
Choose a quiet nature or abstract built-in image
Try a light Mint-Y style and a simple built-in icon set
Keep it at the bottom and set a comfortable row size around 38 to 42 pixels


Dark coding desktop
Choose a darker built-in image with little visual clutter
Try a built-in dark Mint-Y style and readable icons
Move it to the top or keep it at the bottom, then make it slightly taller


Easy-to-see desktop
Choose an uncluttered image that does not hide labels
Choose the clearest high-contrast built-in style available
Increase the row size to about 46 to 52 pixels and keep the menu, network, sound, and clock easy to find






Example of a clean customized Xfce desktop with a calm wallpaper, tidy File Manager, readable Terminal, and a simple bottom panel.


This course example shows one possible finished direction. Your design should reflect your own choices and remain readable.



3. Make the three required changes
Use the settings already included with Linux Mint. Do not download themes, packages, or desktop effects without teacher permission. The optional course scripts below are the only approved appearance scripts for this activity.








Change
Linux Mint Cinnamon
Linux Mint Xfce




Wallpaper
Right-click the desktop and choose Change Desktop Background
Right-click the desktop and choose Desktop Settings


Theme or icons
Open System Settings > Themes
Open Settings > Appearance


Panel
Open System Settings > Panel, or right-click the panel
Right-click the panel and choose Panel > Panel Preferences



The screenshots below show Xfce. Cinnamon students use the matching Cinnamon path in the table.

Change A: wallpaper



Xfce Desktop Settings open to the Background controls and wallpaper choices.



Right-click an empty part of the desktop.
Select Desktop Settings, then Background.
Choose a different built-in picture. Close the window to see the result.

Example: choose a simple image whose light and dark areas still let you read desktop icon labels. Screenshot source: It’s FOSS.


Change B: theme or icons



Xfce Appearance settings open to the Style tab with several built-in themes.



Open Menu > Settings > Appearance. If you cannot find it, type Appearance into the menu search box.
Open the Style tab and try a different built-in style. This changes application windows, menus, buttons, and colours.
You may also open the Icons tab and choose a different built-in icon set. Keep labels and controls readable.

Example: compare one light and one dark Mint-Y variant, then keep the one that gives better contrast with your wallpaper. Screenshot source: Xfce Project.


Change C: panel



Xfce Panel Preferences showing the Display tab and Row size control.



Right-click the bottom panel, which is the bar with the menu and clock.
Choose Panel > Panel Preferences. You can also search for Panel in the menu.
Change the Row size first. A small change, such as 36 pixels to 42 pixels, is easy to see and easy to reverse.
If you want another change, move the panel to the top or adjust its appearance. Close Panel Preferences when finished.

Do not delete the panel or remove the application menu, network, sound, or clock controls. Screenshot source: It’s FOSS.
If a setting looks wrong, return to the same settings window and change it back. If you cannot restore the panel or essential controls, stop and ask for help.


Optional shortcut for Cinnamon
The Cinnamon script is designed for Linux Mint Cinnamon, including Cinnamon 5.6 on Linux Mint 21.1. It changes only a small set of current-user appearance settings. It does not use sudo, install software, download themes, remove applets, or modify personal files.
It first shows a preview. If you continue, it creates a backup and requires you to type APPLY. Its menu also provides a Restore option.
Download tej-cinnamon-style.sh
Run one command at a time:
INPUT
cd ~/Downloads
INPUT
less tej-cinnamon-style.sh
Press q to leave less.
INPUT
chmod +x tej-cinnamon-style.sh
INPUT
./tej-cinnamon-style.sh
Choose the Windows-style or Mac-inspired preview. Read the proposed changes, then type APPLY only if you want them. Choose Restore from the menu to return to the most recent settings saved by the course script.
The script supports one Cinnamon panel. If it detects multiple panels, it stops without changing anything and directs you to use System Settings > Panel manually.
The panel and window-setting names come from the official Cinnamon settings schema and official window settings module.


Optional shortcut for Xfce
After you save the required BEFORE screenshot, you may use the course appearance script on Linux Mint Xfce only. It changes settings for your account without sudo, saves a backup of the current Xfce configuration, and offers two starting points:

Windows-style: a full-width bottom panel with larger controls and desktop icons.
Mac-inspired: a centred, auto-hiding bottom panel with larger launcher icons and window buttons on the left.

The presets are starting points, not copies of Windows or macOS. You still decide whether the result is readable and useful.
The script uses Xfce’s own xfconf-query tool, following the same general approach documented by the Xfce Project and used in Linux Mint community customization scripts. This course version changes only a small, checked set of visual settings.
Open Terminal and run one command at a time:
INPUT
cd ~/Downloads
INPUT
curl -fLO https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/assets/linux/tej-xfce-style.sh
Inspect the script before running it:
INPUT
less tej-xfce-style.sh
Press q to leave less. Then make the script executable and run it:
INPUT
chmod +x tej-xfce-style.sh
INPUT
./tej-xfce-style.sh
Choose option 1 or 2. Take the required AFTER screenshot only after you have checked that the menu, network, sound, and clock are still easy to use.






TipChange values and see what happens



The script creates ~/.config/tej-xfce-style.conf. Open it in Linux Mint’s text editor:
xed ~/.config/tej-xfce-style.conf
Try changing one value, save the file, run ./tej-xfce-style.sh again, and choose option 3. For example, PANEL_SIZE=52 makes the panel taller, PANEL_LENGTH=90 makes it shorter, and DESKTOP_ICON_SIZE=64 makes desktop icons larger. Keep panel length from 40 to 100 and do not remove required controls.




Configuration detective: predict, test, and solve
Do not stop at copying commands. Use the script as a small problem-solving experiment:

Run ./tej-xfce-style.sh and choose option 4 to record the current values.
Pick one safe variable in ~/.config/tej-xfce-style.conf. Before editing it, write what you predict will change and what should stay the same.
Change only that variable in xed, save the file, rerun the script, and choose option 3.
Compare the result with your prediction. If it did not work as expected, read the terminal message, choose option 4 again, and check the spelling and allowed range in the configuration file.
Use the built-in help instead of waiting for the next instruction:

INPUT
xfconf-query --help
Then inspect the panel settings and their current values:
INPUT
xfconf-query -c xfce4-panel -l -v
Find the property that matches the variable you changed. Explain what the channel, property, and value represent. The Xfce xfconf-query guide explains the command options, and the Xfce Panel guide explains panel size, length, and hiding behaviour.






ImportantIndependent problem-solving challenge



Make one useful change that is not given as an exact value above. State your goal, predict the result, test it, and explain what you changed after seeing the result. If the first attempt fails, describe the evidence you used to correct it. Do not use sudo, delete a panel, remove required controls, or run an unfamiliar command that changes files.





4. Save your AFTER screenshot
Make sure the updated wallpaper and panel are visible. You may leave File Manager open so the theme is also visible. Take another screenshot and insert it into the same Google Doc.


5. Answer all five reflection questions
In your assignment Google Doc, answer:

What wallpaper did you choose, and where did you change it?
What theme or icon change did you make, and which setting did you use?
What did you change about the panel, and how did you do it?
Which change made the desktop look better or easier to use, and why?
What did you predict, test, and learn from your configuration change? If something went wrong, explain the evidence you used to fix it.







NoteOptional customization



After completing the required work, you may change fonts or pointer size, add a favourite application shortcut, arrange desktop icons, or investigate another built-in appearance setting. Do not install a theme or desktop effect without permission.

Extension work: network and software exploration

Install approved software

You may also choose one school-appropriate game or useful application, read its description and system requirements, and ask for approval before installing it.

title: Set Up Your Accounts and Explore Linux
text:
3.1 Computer Detective






TipLEVEL 4+: MAKE THE INSTRUCTIONS BETTER



If anything here is unclear, incomplete, or could be explained better, improve it in your own copy. Use Suggesting mode if it is available. Otherwise, add a clearly labelled “Suggested improvement” with your revised wording. Include one sentence explaining why your version is clearer or more useful. Do not remove required work. Mr. A will review your change and may update the course website and future assignment documents if he agrees it helps. Improving a real instruction accurately is one way to demonstrate Level 4+ thinking.



Part 5: meet the terminal






ImportantOpen the assignment and know what to submit



Make a copy of 3.1 Computer Detective: Terminal Quest.
Submit ONE completed Google Doc in Google Classroom. Paste the complete, reviewed command history into that document. Do not submit a separate history text file.








NoteTwo ways to keep working



At home: complete Computer Detective on Windows with WSL or Git Bash, Mac, a Chromebook Linux environment, Linux, Android, or iPhone/iPad.
In class without Internet: complete it after Linux Mint is installed or while Linux Mint is running from the bootable USB. The core commands work offline. Download the TEJ Linux Offline Kit before disconnecting for offline assignment and answer-sheet copies. Making Ethernet cables and bringing every computer online will take time, so this work is ready while you wait.




1. Open the correct terminal

Windows with WSL
Open Start and search for WSL, Ubuntu, or the name of the installed Linux distribution. Open the matching app. Run the Linux assignment commands there, not in PowerShell.
If WSL is not installed, ask the computer owner or teacher for permission. Installation requires administrator access and may require a restart. With permission, open PowerShell as Administrator and run:
INPUT
wsl --install
Restart if Windows asks. If installation is blocked, a security warning appears, or you are unsure which distribution opened, stop and ask for help. Follow the official Microsoft WSL installation guide when needed.


Windows with Git Bash
With the computer owner’s permission, install Git for Windows and open Git Bash from Start. Git Bash provides Bash, Git, and common Unix-style commands inside Windows.
Git Bash is useful, but it is not Linux or Unix. Windows still supplies the file system, permissions, processes, and system information. Paths, available commands, and outputs can therefore differ from WSL, Linux, or macOS. Use Git Bash for file navigation, Git, shell practice, scripts, and Bashcrawl. If a Computer Detective step needs a Linux process tool, use the Windows alternative given in that step.


Linux Mint or Ubuntu
Press Ctrl + Alt + T, or search the application menu for Terminal. WSL is not needed on a Linux computer.


Mac
Press Command + Space, search for Terminal, and press Return. You can also open Applications > Utilities > Terminal.


Chromebook with the Linux development environment
On a personal Chromebook or an owner account, open Settings > About ChromeOS > Developers. Beside Linux development environment, select Set up and follow the prompts. Setup needs Internet and can take several minutes. When it finishes, open Terminal from the Launcher and select the Linux terminal.
A school-managed Chromebook may hide or block this feature. Do not remove management, change security settings, or use Developer Mode. Use another supported device if the normal Linux development environment is unavailable. Follow the official Google Chromebook Linux setup guide when needed.


Android phone or tablet
Install Termux from F-Droid, then open Termux. Do not use the outdated Play Store build. The assignment commands work directly in Termux.


iPhone or iPad
Install iSH Shell. Open iSH and run these commands one at a time so the remaining instructions use Bash:
INPUT
apk update
INPUT
apk add bash
INPUT
bash
Using a phone is slower and more difficult than using a computer, but Android and iPhone both work. A Bluetooth keyboard makes it easier. If you are waiting for a classroom computer or Internet connection, use your phone to begin or continue the assignment instead of doing nothing. 📱💻



2. Identify the account and current folder
Run one command at a time. Read the result and enter the requested answer in your Google Doc.
INPUT
whoami
INPUT
hostname
INPUT
pwd
INPUT
ls
INPUT
ls -a
EXAMPLE OUTPUT
Desktop  Documents  Downloads  Music  Pictures
Your username, computer name, path, files, and hidden items will differ. A shell prompt may end with $ or %; do not type that prompt symbol as part of a command.


3. Investigate the operating system
INPUT
uname -s
INPUT
uname -m
INPUT
df -h .
Find the row for the filesystem containing the current folder. Record the value in the Avail column from that row. Do not copy a value from another row such as tmpfs. The device name is different on different computers, so it may not be /dev/sda2.
INPUT
uptime
Record the system name, machine or CPU type, available space, and uptime in your Google Doc. On a Mac, the system name may be Darwin. In WSL, the system name is normally Linux because Linux is running inside Windows.


4. Create the terminal-quest folder and hello.txt
Start at the file-system root so you can see the move. Run each command separately and press Enter after every command. cd means change directory, pwd means print working directory, and ~ means the signed-in user’s home folder.
INPUT
cd /
INPUT
pwd
Now return to your home folder and check the location again:
INPUT
cd ~/
INPUT
pwd
Compare the two results. cd / moves to the root of the file system. cd ~/ returns to your own home folder.
INPUT
mkdir -p terminal-quest
INPUT
cd terminal-quest
INPUT
pwd
INPUT
echo Hello from my computer > hello.txt
INPUT
ls
INPUT
cat hello.txt
EXAMPLE OUTPUT
Hello from my computer
Return to your home folder and confirm your location:
INPUT
cd ~
INPUT
pwd


5. View running processes
On WSL, Linux Mint, or Ubuntu, try:
INPUT
htop
If htop is not installed, use top, or ask permission before installing software. On Ubuntu-based systems, the approved installation commands are:
INPUT
sudo apt update
INPUT
sudo apt install htop -y
On a Mac, use htop only if it is already installed. Otherwise run:
INPUT
top
Press q to leave htop or top. Observe one CPU and one memory detail. Never end an unfamiliar process. If installation is blocked or asks for access you do not have, use top and ask for help.
On Android with Termux or iPhone/iPad with iSH, use top. Press q to leave it. Do not try to stop unfamiliar phone processes.
In Git Bash, top and htop are not normally included. Run tasklist | more, or open Windows Task Manager, then record one running process and one CPU or memory observation. This difference is useful evidence that Git Bash is a Windows shell environment rather than a Linux system.


6. Review and copy the complete command history
History contains commands, not their output. Review it before copying. Remove or redact passwords, tokens, personal names, private paths, Wi-Fi credentials, and other private information. If you see a password or token, do not paste it. Stop and ask for help, and change any exposed credential.

Windows WSL, Windows Git Bash, Linux Mint, or Ubuntu using Bash
Review the history:
INPUT
history
On Windows WSL or Git Bash, copy the complete history to the Windows clipboard:
INPUT
history | clip.exe
On Linux Mint or Ubuntu, first check the desktop session:
INPUT
echo $XDG_SESSION_TYPE
If the result is x11, ask permission to install xclip if needed, then copy:
INPUT
sudo apt install xclip -y
INPUT
history | xclip -selection clipboard
If the result is wayland, ask permission to install wl-clipboard if needed, then copy:
INPUT
sudo apt install wl-clipboard -y
INPUT
history | wl-copy


Mac using the default zsh shell
Review the complete history:
INPUT
history 1
Copy it to the Mac clipboard:
INPUT
history 1 | pbcopy
If the Mac uses Bash instead of zsh, use history and history | pbcopy.


Android or iPhone/iPad using Bash
Review the complete history:
INPUT
history
Touch and hold in the terminal, select the reviewed history, and copy it. If the output is long, save it to a file and display it before selecting the text:
INPUT
history > ~/terminal-quest-history.txt
INPUT
cat ~/terminal-quest-history.txt
Switch to your Google Doc, touch and hold in the FULL COMMAND HISTORY box, and choose Paste. Remove private information before submitting.
Paste the complete, reviewed history into the labelled box in your Terminal Quest Google Doc. Confirm that it includes the activities you tried. Review the pasted text again before submitting. Submit only that completed Google Doc.






TipBonus: compare a second operating system



Repeat Sections 1 and 2 on a second operating system and explain one meaningful difference in the output. You may use another physical computer, a Linux Mint live USB, or VirtualBox inside Windows, Mac, or Linux. Ask the computer owner before installing software, and do not change firmware, security, or virtualization settings without permission. This is worth up to 5 bonus marks.

title: Set Up Your Accounts and Explore Linux
text:
3.2 Bashcrawl






TipLEVEL 4+: MAKE THE INSTRUCTIONS BETTER



If anything here is unclear, incomplete, or could be explained better, improve it in your own copy. Use Suggesting mode if it is available. Otherwise, add a clearly labelled “Suggested improvement” with your revised wording. Include one sentence explaining why your version is clearer or more useful. Do not remove required work. Mr. A will review your change and may update the course website and future assignment documents if he agrees it helps. Improving a real instruction accurately is one way to demonstrate Level 4+ thinking.



Part 6: clone and play Bashcrawl






ImportantOpen the assignment and know what to submit



Make a copy of 3.2 Bashcrawl Terminal Adventure.
Submit ONE completed Google Doc with all four reflection answers and at least one readable terminal screenshot. No history file is required.








NoteAt home or offline in class



At home: Bashcrawl works through Windows WSL, Windows Git Bash, Mac, a Chromebook Linux environment, Linux, Android, or iPhone/iPad.
In class without Internet: after Linux Mint is installed or while it is running from the bootable USB, copy the included bashcrawl folder from the TEJ Linux Offline Kit and play without downloading anything.


Bashcrawl is a terminal adventure. Folders are rooms and files contain clues. There is no required final room and no time limit. Explore for as long as you can, return another day if you want, and record the furthest room you reached.


1. Open Terminal and check Git

Windows WSL: Open Ubuntu or the installed Linux distribution from Start.
Windows Git Bash: With the computer owner’s permission, install Git for Windows and open Git Bash. Git Bash is not Linux or Unix, but the Bashcrawl commands used here are mostly the same.
Linux Mint or Ubuntu: Press Ctrl + Alt + T, or open Terminal from the application menu.
Mac: Press Command + Space, search for Terminal, and press Return.
Chromebook: Open the Linux Terminal from the Launcher. If Linux is not already enabled, use Settings > About ChromeOS > Developers > Linux development environment > Set up on a personal or owner account. A school-managed Chromebook may block this feature.

On a Chromebook, extract the offline kit in the Files app. Move the complete bashcrawl folder into Linux files, then move it into ~/Games from Terminal before starting the game. Linux setup requires Internet once, but the included Bashcrawl folder can be played offline afterward.
The core Bashcrawl commands are mostly the same in WSL, Git Bash, Linux, macOS, ChromeOS Linux, Termux, and iSH: ls, cd, pwd, cat, and git clone. The prompt, home-folder path, permissions, and available system commands may differ.

Use a phone or tablet
You can also play Bashcrawl on a phone or tablet if you have access to one.

Android: Install Termux from F-Droid. Open Termux, then run these commands one at a time:

INPUT
pkg update
INPUT
pkg install git

title: Git: Save the History of Your Work
text:
Your first repository
Create a teacher-approved project folder inside your home directory. Configure Git with the classroom identity supplied by your teacher. Do not publish a personal email address.
mkdir -p ~/linux-labs/my-site
cd ~/linux-labs/my-site
git init
printf "# My Technology Site\n" > README.md
git status
git add README.md
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Add project README"
git log --oneline
Repeat the cycle after making one small change: edit, git status, review, stage, review the staged change, commit, and inspect the history.

title: Git: Save the History of Your Work
section: Use Git with notebooks and websites
text:
Use Git with notebooks and websites
Commit source files that another person needs to reproduce the work: .qmd, Markdown, configuration, code, small approved datasets, notebooks, and licensed assets. Do not commit Quarto’s generated _site or .quarto folders for the classroom starter. Do not commit virtual environments, passwords, tokens, class codes, private student evidence, or restricted teacher resources.
Before every commit:
git status
git diff
git diff --staged
Use git add with the intended paths, then inspect the staged diff. A useful commit contains one understandable change and a message that explains it.

title: Git: Save the History of Your Work
text:
The problem
git status shows an unfamiliar generated file and a notebook containing output you did not intend to share.
The challenge: decide what is source, what is generated, and what is private. Update .gitignore only for a repeatable file pattern, not to hide a mistake after it has been committed.






TipHints






Ask whether another person needs the file to reproduce the project.
Use git diff --staged before committing and git check-ignore -v path/to/file to explain an ignored file.
If a secret was committed, stop and tell the teacher; deleting the current file does not remove it from earlier history.

title: Git: Save the History of Your Work
text:
Common issues







Problem
Check




Git asks for identity
Use the teacher-approved classroom identity. Do not invent or publish a private email address.


Everything is in one large commit
Unstage safely with git restore --staged <path>, then stage one coherent change.


Line endings appear changed
Confirm the actual content and classroom Git configuration before committing a mass rewrite.


Merge conflict markers appear
Do not delete them blindly. Compare both versions, keep the correct combined content, test, then stage the resolution.

title: Install Linux Mint 22.3 Xfce
text:
Before you begin
You need:

the assigned classroom computer;
a Linux Mint 22.3 “Zena” Xfce USB installer signed out from your teacher;
the classroom Wi-Fi credentials; and
your copy of the Linux Mint Installation Reflection.

Disconnect any personal USB drives or external storage. Have the teacher confirm the target computer before you erase anything.

How the classroom USB was made
The teacher, with help from student volunteers, prepared the bootable USB drives before this lab. They downloaded the Linux Mint Xfce .iso image from the official Linux Mint download page and used balenaEtcher to write the image to a USB drive. On Windows, Rufus is another good tool for creating a bootable USB.
An ISO cannot simply be copied onto a USB like an ordinary file. A tool such as Etcher or Rufus writes the image in a form the computer can start from. This process erases the USB drive, so do not try it with a personal drive unless its contents are safely backed up.
For this lab, sign out a prepared USB from your teacher. Record its number if your class uses numbered drives, and return it when the installation is complete.


Working at home: Windows and Mac options
In class, we are installing Linux Mint directly on approved classroom computers. Do not erase or dual boot a family computer for this course.
If you use Windows 11 or a supported Windows 10 computer at home, the recommended option is Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL 2) with Ubuntu. It gives you a real Linux command line without replacing Windows. Ask the computer owner for permission because installation requires administrator access and may require a restart.

Open PowerShell as Administrator.
Run:

wsl --install

Restart Windows if asked.
Open Ubuntu from the Start menu.
Create a private Linux username and password. The password will not appear while you type it.
Return to PowerShell and verify the installation:

wsl --list --verbose
wsl --status
If WSL is already installed but Ubuntu is missing, run wsl --list --online, then wsl --install -d Ubuntu. Never use wsl --unregister for this course because it permanently deletes that WSL distribution and its files. Follow the official Microsoft WSL installation guide if your screen differs.
On a Mac, use the built-in Terminal for transferable work such as files, Git, Quarto, Python and SSH. macOS is Unix-like, but it is not Linux. Complete Linux-specific hardware, package, permission and administration activities on the classroom Linux computer or an approved remote Linux host. Apple’s Terminal User Guide is a useful reference.

1. Start the live system
Insert the Linux Mint USB drive, then start or restart the computer. You need to choose the USB as the startup device before the existing operating system loads.

On the classroom Intel iMacs and Mac minis

Immediately hold Option (⌥) or Alt until Startup Manager appears.
Select the USB drive (it may appear as EFI Boot) and press Enter/Return. If the USB does not appear, stop and ask your teacher.

Apple documents the Option/Alt startup shortcut in its Intel Mac startup-key guide.


On a Windows PC
The startup key is different for almost every manufacturer and model. Common keys include Delete, F1, F2, F10, F11, F12, and Escape.

Watch the first manufacturer-logo screen for a message such as Boot Menu, Boot Options, Setup, BIOS, or UEFI.
Press the listed key repeatedly as the computer starts. Try the one-time Boot Menu first and select the USB drive.
If there is no boot menu, enter the BIOS/UEFI settings and, with teacher approval, temporarily move the USB drive ahead of the internal drive in the boot order. Do not change unrelated settings.

If the key is not shown, search for manufacturer model boot menu key or manufacturer model boot from USB. Include the exact manufacturer and model printed on the computer. The official Linux Mint boot guide also lists common keys.
Choose the normal Start Linux Mint option when the Linux Mint startup menu appears. Linux Mint first opens a live session: a temporary desktop running from the USB drive.
The live session may feel slower than the finished installation, and changes made there are not permanent. If the live session asks for a password, leave it blank and press Enter.
Double-click Install Linux Mint on the desktop.

5. Choose the installation type
Select Erase disk and install Linux Mint.

Leave Advanced features at its default setting with None selected. We can explore advanced storage settings in a later lab.
Do not select an encryption option for this classroom installation.
Do not select Something else.
Do not select an “install alongside” option in this lab.




Linux Mint installation-type screen with Erase disk and install Linux Mint selected.


Select Install Now or Continue, depending on the wording shown. Read the drive-change summary, confirm that it refers to the approved classroom drive, and then continue.
In a future lab, we will install another operating system alongside Windows and create a dual-boot computer. That is not today’s task.






WarningDual-boot installations use different instructions



If you are installing Linux on your own computer and want to keep Windows, stop here and do not choose “Erase disk and install Linux Mint.” A dual-boot installation requires a current backup, enough free storage, and a careful plan for the computer’s partitions, encryption, firmware, and recovery options.
It is usually easier to install Windows first and Linux second. Windows installation can replace the existing boot sequence, while Linux Mint normally detects Windows and creates a menu for choosing an operating system at startup. See Linux Mint’s official multi-boot guidance.
Before changing partitions, check whether Windows uses BitLocker/device encryption, save its recovery key, and research the exact computer model. An encrypted Windows drive may prevent a Linux installer from safely examining or resizing the Windows partitions. Ubuntu’s BitLocker dual-boot explanation describes this issue clearly.
Some computers have two internal SSDs. Installing each operating system on a separate drive can make the layout easier to understand and can reduce the chance of accidentally changing the other system’s partitions or boot files. However, this is not a rule of EFI/UEFI, and it is not required on every computer. Firmware behaviour varies, even between Lenovo Legion models, so search the manufacturer, exact model, and terms such as dual boot, UEFI, and boot order before proceeding. Use a model-specific guide and ask for experienced help rather than guessing.

Why this is useful
Quarto turns readable plain-text source into a consistent website. It can combine engineering explanations, equations, code, graphs, and project evidence without hand-editing HTML.

text:
What you will make
Download and extract the TEJ Quarto portfolio starter. You will add one project, one category, an accessible image, and a tested relative link. This teaching website is a larger Quarto example; your project stays intentionally small.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
Before you start

Complete Git: Save the History of Your Work.
Install Quarto on an unrestricted computer and run quarto check and git --version.
Read the starter README.md.
Do not place private student information, credentials, classroom codes, or restricted files in the project.

JupyterLite cannot render Quarto websites. Use a local or teacher-authorized hosted environment with the Quarto CLI.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
1. Learn the source structure
quarto-portfolio-starter/
├── _quarto.yml       # project and website configuration
├── index.qmd         # home page source
├── about.qmd         # about page source
├── projects/         # listing page and project pages
├── blog/             # optional posts and listing
├── assets/           # images and downloadable evidence
├── styles.css        # small visual adjustments
└── _site/            # generated output; do not edit
A relative link starts from the file containing the link. From projects/circuit-analysis.qmd, ../assets/circuit-project.svg moves up from projects/, then into assets/.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
2. Write Markdown
# Page title
## Section heading

Write a paragraph with **strong text**, *emphasis*, and a [useful link](https://quarto.org/).

- Use a list for related items.
- Keep units beside measured values.

![Useful description of the evidence](../assets/example.svg)
Use descriptive link text. Alt text should state what a reader needs to notice, not repeat the filename.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
3. Edit YAML safely
YAML front matter sits between --- lines at the top of a page:
---
title: "Motor Current Test"
description: "Compare predicted and measured current during a load test."
date: 2026-01-20
categories: [electronics, motors, measurement]
image: ../assets/motor-test.svg
image-alt: "Current rises as the motor load increases across four measured points."
---
Indent with spaces, keep list items aligned, and quote text containing punctuation when unsure. A render error that names a line near the page top often indicates malformed YAML.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
4. Configure the website
_quarto.yml sets project-wide behaviour. The starter uses a navbar, local full-text search, a Cosmo theme, shared CSS, a footer, and _site output.
website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: projects/index.qmd
        text: Projects
  search:
    location: navbar
    type: overlay
Use the official navigation guide if you need a sidebar for a larger site. Do not add a sidebar merely to imitate this course website.
Change the theme through the documented format.html.theme option. Keep readable contrast, visible keyboard focus, responsive layout, and consistent headings. Test at a narrow window width before adding custom CSS.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
5. Add a project listing
The starter’s projects/index.qmd uses Quarto’s native listing:
listing:
  contents: "*.qmd"
  type: grid
  grid-columns: 2
  sort: "date desc"
  sort-ui: [date, title]
  filter-ui: [title, description, categories]
  categories: true
Each project contributes its title, description, date, categories, and image through YAML. Quarto builds the responsive card grid, filter box, category controls, and sort controls. No custom JavaScript is required.
To add a category, add a term to one project’s categories list and render. To change default order, change sort using the official listing documentation.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
6. Use the optional blog
The blog/ folder demonstrates dated posts and categories. Add a post by copying a file in blog/posts/, changing its metadata, and writing the note. To remove the blog, remove its navbar entry, delete the folder, render, and verify navigation and search. The starter README records the same procedure.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
7. Preview, render, and commit
quarto preview
Preview after one small change. Stop the preview with Ctrl+C. Then build the complete static site:
quarto render
Test the home page, project grid, category filter, sort control, search, images, and every changed link. Inspect the terminal for warnings.
git status
git diff
git add _quarto.yml index.qmd about.qmd projects blog assets styles.css README.md .gitignore
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Add tested engineering portfolio project"
Adjust the file list to match your intended changes. Do not add _site, .quarto, secrets, or private evidence.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
The problem
Your new project does not appear correctly: its image is broken, its category is missing, or the render stops.
The essential skill: use the first specific error, inspect the named source, make one change, and render again.
The challenge: add one project and category, change the project ordering, repair one broken image and relative link, and explain how you found the correct Quarto option.
The stumbling block: YAML indentation and relative paths can look plausible while pointing to a different structure than the rendered site expects.
The investigation: search the official Quarto website guide, listing guide, and search guide using the exact option or error text.






TipHint 1: concept clue





Separate the failure: configuration, page metadata, file path, or page content.









TipHint 2: documentation clue





Search for Quarto listing sort-ui filter-ui categories or the exact YAML key named by the error.









TipHint 3: technical clue





Validate YAML spacing, confirm filename capitalization, then count folder levels from the page containing the relative link.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
Check your work

quarto render completes without an unexplained warning.
Search finds text from the new project.
The listing filters by its new category and sorts by the selected field.
Images load at desktop and narrow widths and have useful alt text.
Internal links work from the rendered site.
git status shows only intended source files.

title: Build a Website with Quarto
text:
Save and submit
Keep the complete source project. Submit a teacher-approved ZIP or repository plus a screenshot of the local rendered result and git log --oneline. Publishing is optional; if assigned, continue to Publish Your Quarto Site with GitHub Pages.
